summary: Milestone 2026.05.257 had 0 experiments committed to the timing window — the thirty-second consecutive empty-timing-window retro. No zero-artifact alarm: conductor can activate a milestone and proceed to retro generation without emitting any experiment commits, burning a milestone slot with zero research output.
Retro task fires at or immediately after activation, before any substantive experiment has time to complete — structural ordering flaw in the conductor's milestone close sequence.
improvements_suggested: Fix timing-script look-back to use conductor-state.json activation timestamp as the deterministic lower bound (eliminates root cause of the 32-milestone zero-execution streak).

Wire a zero-artifact alarm: if no experiment result JSON lands in results/ within 60 minutes of milestone activation, emit a conductor alert and hold retro generation until at least one experiment completes.
Introduce a milestone-open sentinel commit at activation time — a zero-content commit whose timestamp gives the timing script a reliable anchor independent of experiment arrival.
Schedule the retro task as the LAST item in the milestone's task queue, not the first, so it can only fire after earlier tasks have had a chance to produce artifacts.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Fix timing-script look-back to conductor-state.json activation timestamp — eliminates root cause of the 32-milestone zero-execution streak in a single one-line change to the timing query.
Wire zero-artifact alarm at 60 min post-activation — structural backstop that prevents the conductor from closing a milestone with 0 experiments when the root-cause fix has not yet landed.

Activate at least one non-retro GGUF inference experiment in the same session as milestone activation — breaks the zero-execution streak with no structural changes required; both RTX 3090s are healthy and waiting.
